correctness.rationale: For each nonroot edge the indicator of being spanned by a size-k leaf sample is 1 minus its avoidance indicator. Summing and expanding pairs recovers the exact displayed first and second raw moments from clade-size counts a_s and pair-union counts b_s. Binomial coefficients in k=n-j form a triangular system with nonzero diagonal, so both moment profiles are equivalent to (a,b), with b_n set by the total edge-pair count. The independent canonical non-plane rooted-tree recursion enumerated all sizes 1..16 (10905 shapes at 16) and the independently coded bit-clade pair signatures had a single duplicate class at 16 and none below; that class is the stated nonisomorphic assortative/mixed pair. Independent two-leaf enumeration gave third binomial-moment sums 5909 and 5910, difference 1/120. Attaching a new root with an extra leaf keeps all old a,b entries and adds only universal clades, preserving collisions for n>16. Proved scope is unit-edge non-plane full binary shapes; no claim of uniqueness of larger-n collisions or weighted-tree identification. Finite exhaustive search is valid for exactly n<=16, not an infinite uniqueness proof.
